name: Fred’s Peak (2nd Walk)
description:
𝑰𝑴𝑷𝑶𝑹𝑻𝑨𝑵𝑻 𝑵𝑶𝑻𝑬 𝑨𝑩𝑶𝑼𝑻 𝑹𝑺𝑽𝑷𝒔 : 𝑺𝒆𝒍𝒆𝒄𝒕𝒊𝒏𝒈 '𝑮𝒐𝒊𝒏𝒈' 𝒐𝒏 𝑭𝒂𝒄𝒆𝒃𝒐𝒐𝒌 𝒅𝒐𝒆𝒔𝒏'𝒕 𝒄𝒐𝒖𝒏𝒕 𝒂𝒔 𝒂𝒏 𝑹𝑺𝑽𝑷. 𝑷𝒍𝒆𝒂𝒔𝒆 𝒄𝒉𝒆𝒄𝒌 𝒕𝒉𝒆 𝒅𝒆𝒔𝒄𝒓𝒊𝒑𝒕𝒊𝒐𝒏 𝒇𝒐𝒓 𝒕𝒉𝒆 𝑪𝒍𝒖𝒃'𝒔 𝑹𝑺𝑽𝑷 𝒑𝒓𝒐𝒄𝒆𝒔𝒔.

Sun, 25th August
Leader - Wilfred Karnoll

Rated - Off-track, remote. Difficulty level - 5.
This is a vertical walk with rock scrambling across sheer rock faces vertically.

If you are scared of heights - this walk is not for you. This is an exposed walk in places.

Duration - this will be a 6-8 hour day depending on the group.
The walk itself begins on a dirt road that will take us to the rocky outcrops known by the rock climbers as the pinnacles. From there we will follow a reasonably well defined (in some places ill-defined) track that takes us past other beautiful rock faces and then eventually out to the rear of Frederick's Peak. We climb up a steep gully that is known to contain stinging trees. Be warned - they do bite. At the top of the gully we turn right and make our way carefully to the top. There are spectacular views of Townsville, the Dam and Harvey's Range, as well as the Islands on a clear day. 

Bring a jacket as it could well be windy and cold at the top. We'll enjoy lunch there and make our way back via the way we came.

RSVP Process:
TBWC members - Free. $5 for Visitors/Guests.
By direct communication with Wilfred Karnoll - wilfred.suzanne@bigpond.com.
We need to balance the number of 4wd available to the number of people.

name: Killymoon Creek
description:
𝑰𝑴𝑷𝑶𝑹𝑻𝑨𝑵𝑻 𝑵𝑶𝑻𝑬 𝑨𝑩𝑶𝑼𝑻 𝑹𝑺𝑽𝑷𝒔 : 𝑺𝒆𝒍𝒆𝒄𝒕𝒊𝒏𝒈 '𝑮𝒐𝒊𝒏𝒈' 𝒐𝒏 𝑭𝒂𝒄𝒆𝒃𝒐𝒐𝒌 𝒅𝒐𝒆𝒔𝒏'𝒕 𝒄𝒐𝒖𝒏𝒕 𝒂𝒔 𝒂𝒏 𝑹𝑺𝑽𝑷. 𝑷𝒍𝒆𝒂𝒔𝒆 𝒄𝒉𝒆𝒄𝒌 𝒕𝒉𝒆 𝒅𝒆𝒔𝒄𝒓𝒊𝒑𝒕𝒊𝒐𝒏 𝒇𝒐𝒓 𝒕𝒉𝒆 𝑪𝒍𝒖𝒃'𝒔 𝑹𝑺𝑽𝑷 𝒑𝒓𝒐𝒄𝒆𝒔𝒔.

Sunday, 18th August 2024
Leader: Molly

Rated: 3-4. Not easy, but manageable for those who don’t mind a creek based walk.

About:
Killymoon Creek, in the dry season, is a fantastic spot for rock-hopping enthusiasts. This walk start on a fire trail on private property with a few good hills to get everyone warmed up. The creek bed starts as a series of small rocky gullies which soon open up into a spectacular gorge. 

We will take lunch at the swimming hole, where the polar bears amongst us can have a dip before lunch. This will be our turn around point and we will descend back down the creek from here.

This adventure will see us tackling numerous kinds of climbing. You will need to have a suitable level of fitness and coordination.

How long:
Full day walk. Estimate back at the car park around 4 pm.

name: TBWC Meet & Greet + Walk Briefings
description:
TBWC Meet & Greet + Walk Briefings
Monday, 12th August, 2024
Time: 6:00 pm to 6:30 pm

Location: At the Club house which is at Blessed Mary Mackillop Parish meeting room (building behind the Church), 43 Ross River Road Mundingburra. Take the St Joseph School entrance.

name: Mt Elliot
description:
𝑰𝑴𝑷𝑶𝑹𝑻𝑨𝑵𝑻 𝑵𝑶𝑻𝑬 𝑨𝑩𝑶𝑼𝑻 𝑹𝑺𝑽𝑷𝒔 : 𝑺𝒆𝒍𝒆𝒄𝒕𝒊𝒏𝒈 '𝑮𝒐𝒊𝒏𝒈' 𝒐𝒏 𝑭𝒂𝒄𝒆𝒃𝒐𝒐𝒌 𝒅𝒐𝒆𝒔𝒏'𝒕 𝒄𝒐𝒖𝒏𝒕 𝒂𝒔 𝒂𝒏 𝑹𝑺𝑽𝑷. 𝑷𝒍𝒆𝒂𝒔𝒆 𝒄𝒉𝒆𝒄𝒌 𝒕𝒉𝒆 𝒅𝒆𝒔𝒄𝒓𝒊𝒑𝒕𝒊𝒐𝒏 𝒇𝒐𝒓 𝒕𝒉𝒆 𝑪𝒍𝒖𝒃'𝒔 𝑹𝑺𝑽𝑷 𝒑𝒓𝒐𝒄𝒆𝒔𝒔.

Overnighter - Sat 10 and Sun 11 Aug
Leaders: Brent Campbell , Graeme Taylor & Molly Hoey

Rated: Hard - rough terrain, steep climbs and some creek based walking.
Experienced Hikers only please.

Walk Description:
This hike is epic in it’s beauty and the journey through the belly of the Bowling Green Bay NP. It is best enjoyed as a 2 day trip to enjoy the summit. The route is to be decided, but it is likely that we will take the North Creek Ridgeline route.

Please note - you will need to be self sufficient - carry enough water to last you the day (there will be opportunities to fill up at the lower creeks, but none at the top most likely). You will need to carry your sleep and shelter gear + food and first aid gear).

Molly will email all you need in the email to RSVPd participants.

RSVP: Normally for overnighters, we prefer to meet you at the club meet & greets.

However, the timing of this walk will not suit this -So RSVP via the link below:
https://forms.gle/gS6xdzLk1L87FssJ9
